newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond supply capped by holiday, Tues FOMC meet.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond supply capped by holiday, Tues FOMC meet.

text.p: Primary market supply dried up on Monday amid the widespread Pentecost holiday in Continental Europe, dealers said.
Caution ahead of the eagerly awaited U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting on Tuesday also kept a lid on activity.

A new Reuters poll released Monday morning showed that 21 of 39 primary dealers were calling for no change in policy and the dollar's tight ranges reflected the market's uncertainty about the Fed's intentions.
Meanwhile, on Monday the Daily Mail and General Trust Plc offered to buy back the 48 million stg outstanding on its 5.75 percent 2003 bond exchangeable into Reuters shares.
Daily Mail will issue a new bond due 2004, which will be exchangeable into Reuters shares.
J.P. Morgan Securities will arrange/lead manage the two separate Daily Mail transactions.
The repurchase price of the 2003 bonds will be at an indicated six to eight percent premium over the market price.
The outstanding bond was issued in September 1993 at an exchange price of 4.795 stg per share.
In the emerging market sector, Pakistan's well-flagged three-year dollar FRN will be launched on Tuesday, sources close to the deal said.
The FRN is expected to be for around $200 million at around 400 basis points over LIBOR. ANZ Investment Bank is lead manager.
Slovenia's debut mark Eurobond will be launched within the next two weeks via joint lead managers CSFB and Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.
The deal is expected to be for around 300 million marks with a seven or 10-year maturity. Investor presentations started in London today and will move to Zurich and Frankfurt.
